notes: Day 6 sits at the flat center of the plateau: day 5 (58%) and day 7 (49%) bracket it, and every lever here reads as one step along that slide rather than a new idea.

items.rationale: Day 6 is the last flat day before the day 7 slide begins, so it should cost the player 2 points off day 5's 58% by tightening the cheapest levers only, not by moving the silhouette. greed: 0.94 (day 5) to 0.98, the smallest lever, already most of the push needed since day 5 to day 7 only spans 0.94 to 0.99. abilityFreq: 0.55 to 0.60, the second-smallest lever, one step toward day 7's 0.65. oppRam holds at 7, unchanged from day 5 and day 7 both, so it is not the lever doing work this day. headStart holds at 2, matching day 5; it does not climb to day 7's 3 until the grid itself grows to 11x11, so grid and headStart move together, not here. grid holds at 11x9, day 5's silhouette, since minCost (20, unchanged from day 5) scales with area and this day is not the one that spends that budget. parFlat steps down 4 to 3, continuing the day 4-to-9 taper (4,4,3,2,2,1) toward day 7's 2. slag ticks 0.21 to 0.22, patchDrop falls 0.18 to 0.16, both continuing their day-over-day drift as the run's back half asks for more self-sufficiency. jobTiers is the one deliberate flat spot in the shape: 3,3,3 against day 5's 2,3,3 and day 7's 3,3,4, three identical tier-3 tickets with no spike, because day 6 is the day that should feel like a wall of same-weight work before day 7 introduces its first tier-4 spike. minPd rises 9 to 10, matching the greed and abilityFreq step so the opening route costs a beat more than day 5 without yet reaching day 7's 10 (held flat) plus grid growth.
